Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with wheezing and shortness of breath.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: Patient: So, um, recently I'm wheezy. Uh, I have feel like kind of short of breath.

History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: Mmm, two, three days. Yeah, quite recently.
Patient: Yeah, so I have, I have cough and cough a lot, and I have a fever.
Patient: Yes, I checked, I have fever .

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient experiences exertional dyspnea limiting walking to work.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: I also used to walk to work but recently I can't because it's, I, I feel like very short of breath

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient sometimes finds it difficult to complete sentences due to breathlessness.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Patient: sometimes I feel like I can't even finish sentence is quite difficult to, to complete the, the the talking sometimes, yeah. Occasionally.

Doctor: Right. Have you coughed any phlegm up or anything like that?
Patient: No.

Doctor: Any, any, um, blood in there when you cough?
Patient: No, I don't think so.

Doctor: OK. And any chest pain?
Patient: No chest pain, no.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: No nocturnal symptoms waking the patient.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: Have you been woken up at night time at all?
Patient: No, just daytime working, yeah.

Doctor: Have you been able to do any exercise?
Patient: No, I can't.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Shortness of breath occurs with walking and not at rest; currently feels well at rest.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: OK, and when, at the moment, are you, um, feeling short of breath when you're sitting still? Or just when you walk?
Patient: No.
Patient: Just walk or sometimes, but currently I feel, I feel well.

Doctor: Are you able to get up and down the stairs OK?
Patient: Yeah.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Measured temperature was 37°C and reported as normal.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: What was your temperature?
Patient: Uh, thirty seven, yeah.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient does not have a peak flow meter at home.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: You have what's called a peak flow meter, which you breathe into to get a score on your breathing?
Patient: No, no.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has experienced similar symptoms in the past.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: And have you ever had similar symptoms in the past?
Patient: Um, I think so. It was a while before, yeah, but I can't remember.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Past similar symptoms occurred in adulthood.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text:
Doctor: As, was that as an adult or as a child?
Patient: Sorry? Oh, as a , as a adult, yeah.

Past_Medical_History.source_text:
Doctor: And any problems with wheezing when you were a child or any asthma?
Patient: Uh, yes, I had asthma. I also had, uh, hay fever and eczema , sorry.

Doctor: OK, and when you were a child how bad was your asthma?
Patient: Uh, it's quite bad.

Past_Medical_History.content: Used an asthma inhaler during childhood.
Past_Medical_History.source_text:
Doctor: Did you have to take medication?
Patient: Yeah, I take the asthma inhaler.

Doctor: Do you know which ones you took?
Patient: No, I can't remember.

Past_Medical_History.content: Occasionally required hospital visits for asthma in the past.
Past_Medical_History.source_text:
Doctor: And did you ever have to go to hospital with it?
Patient: Yeah, sometimes.

Past_Medical_History.content: No history of intensive care admission for asthma.
Past_Medical_History.source_text:
Doctor: Did you ever get severely unwell, have to be on intensive care unit or anything like that?
Patient: No, not that bad but still, sometimes, need to go to hospital to check if it goes well.

Past_Medical_History.content: Missed school occasionally due to asthma.
Past_Medical_History.source_text:
Doctor: Did you have to miss school?
Patient: Uh, yeah, occasionally.
Patient: Uh, yes, I had asthma. I also had, uh, hay fever and eczema , sorry.

Doctor: Any other medical problems?
Patient: Uh, I have, uh, hay fever as well.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient reported stopping asthma medication approximately 3–4 years ago.
Past_Medical_History.source_text:
Doctor: OK. And when do you think it last, when do you think that asthma stopped? At what age did you get to a point where you weren't taking medication anymore?
Patient: Few years ago, like, three or four years ago I think? Yeah.

Medications.content: Patient normally uses a salbutamol inhaler.
Medications.source_text:
Doctor: OK, so you, you normally take that do you? Or is that just recently?
Patient: Normally, yeah.

Medications.content: Salbutamol inhaler used approximately every few weeks.
Medications.source_text:
Doctor: OK, and how often do you normally need it?
Patient: Every, every few weeks? I'm not sure.

Doctor: What about when you exercise normally, do you have to use medication? Uh, inhalers?
Patient: Yeah, yeah, a bit.

Medications.content: Patient has an asthma inhaler at home.
Medications.source_text:
Doctor: Have you got an asthma inhaler at home?
Patient: Yeah.

Medications.content: Patient does not have a spacer device at home.
Medications.source_text:
Doctor: Um, do you have a spacer at home?
Patient: No.

Doctor: OK, um, and do you take any other medications?
Patient: No, nothing else.

Medications.content: Does not take medication for hay fever.
Medications.source_text:
Doctor: OK, do you take anything for that?
Patient: No.

Medications.content: Patient uses salbutamol as their inhaler.
Medications.source_text:
Doctor: Have you taken any medication?
Patient: Um, I took salbutamol? Salbutamol? Yeah.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text:
Doctor: And any allergies to medications?
Patient: No, no allergies.

Social_and_Family_History.source_text:
Doctor: Do you smoke?
Patient: No, I don't smoke.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Drinks approximately one glass of wine every two or three days.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text:
Doctor: Every, how often did you say?
Patient: Every two or three days? Depends, yeah.

Doctor: Who do you live with at home?
Patient: I live with my partner.

Doctor: OK, and what's your job, day-to-day?
Patient: Uh, I'm engineer.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Currently working from home or on sick leave due to breathlessness.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: Patient: No I can't because I used to walk walk to work, but recently I, I work from home or sometimes I take sick leave, yeah.

Assessment.source_text: Doctor: Right, OK. Um, I mean, it sounds like you've had a flare up of your asthma.

Assessment.content: Possible trigger is increased pollen exposure.
Assessment.source_text: Doctor: It could be, um, triggered by, if there's more pollen around,

Assessment.content: Possible trigger is a viral infection.
Assessment.source_text: Doctor: or there may be, you may have a viral infection, causing it to get worse.

Plan_of_Care.content: Increase short-acting bronchodilator use to 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: Um, and if you increase it so you're taking it two to four puffs, like, every four hours?
Doctor: OK. Um, what I can do is, I can prescribe you a peak flow meter so we can check your breathing level

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe a spacer device for inhaler use.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: and a spacer to use your inhaler a bit more efficiently,
Doctor: which the pharmacist can show you how you use that when you pick it up.
Doctor: OK, and the other thing to do would be to take a regular antihistamine.

Plan_of_Care.content: Record peak flow in the morning daily over the next week.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: And then if you, when you get the peak flow meter, if you can take, the pharmacist can show you how to use it, and if you can record a value first thing when you wake up.

Plan_of_Care.content: Record peak flow in the evening daily over the next week.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Doctor: And in the evening over the next week,

Follow_up_Information.content: Call back immediately if a high temperature develops or wheezing worsens.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Doctor: Initially, um, if you get a high temperature or your wheezing is getting worse, you need to call us back straightaway so we can just advise you further with that.

Follow_up_Information.content: Arrange an asthma review in about one week.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Doctor: You could arrange a review in a week or so, um, but, but before that and if you're, if you're feeling worse.

Follow_up_Information.content: Plan to discuss recorded peak flow readings over the phone to assess need for additional inhaler.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Doctor: and then we can discuss that over the phone when we look at the figures and see whether you need to go on another inhaler as well.
